boards.idea: The drawer is the whole directory from the first paint, all 25 clubs A to Z beside a map with every pin, and Near me only reorders that list and zooms the map, so nothing is ever hidden and the map and the list can never disagree.
boards.differs: A visitor who never presses Near me simply scrolls: the drawer already holds all 25 clubs in A to Z order beside the map at Louisiana zoom with every pin, and the list is never trimmed to what the map happens to show (Clubs-E's drawer mirrored the viewport, which is why it needed Search this area and its counts). Hovering a card lifts its pin; clicking a pin scrolls the list to its card and selects it. The page has one state, the order of the list: A to Z, or Nearest once a place is known, with a thin 'Farther than 75 miles' divider as the only thing separating near from far. The way back is the ✕ on the location pill (A to Z, state zoom) or the map's All of Louisiana button (zoom out, order kept).
boards.keeps: From Clubs-E: the first screen split into a 460px directory drawer beside a 980px map, 780 tall and sticky; the Louisiana base map (state outline, the Mississippi tab for Picayune, Lake Pontchartrain and the Gulf, the rivers and interstates, grey town labels) with its + − zoom; the 'City, ZIP or club name' field, which locates on a place and narrows on a name; Near me reading location once, on tap, kept only in the address (?near=70808) with a one-tap clear; hover and focus linking card and pin; solid pins for listed meeting times and hollow pins for 'Schedule not listed'; count circles that open on click; 'Fit all clubs', renamed 'All of Louisiana'; the selected card in gold; 'Schedule not listed · Know when they meet? Suggest an update' on the 7 thin clubs; the seven regions with their representatives, open seats covered by LCA admins with Volunteer; Message as a relay form with no address shown; Start a club and Suggest a club as one form with a switch, routed by zip_regions; Suggest an update as one form shared with the club page, with its 'What changed?' chips, Turnstile and sent state; the decided header and footer; the phone's map-plus-sheet pattern; the 25 real clubs with their real towns and meeting lines.
boards.removes: From Clubs-E's first screen, one by one: the '8 clubs within 75 miles of 70808' title and its '5 meet this week · 1 tonight' line; Copy link to this list; the six count chips (Meets today, Weekends, Kids welcome, Rated play, Free, Lessons); the 'Include clubs with no listed schedule' toggle; the three-way sort (Nearest · Meets soonest · A–Z) and the Meets soonest sort with it; the All regions menu; pin numbers and numbered cards; the five-line card and everything on it (logo or initials, club colour dot, region line, Next: line, time-control note, tag chips, Checked month, the Suggest an update and Club page buttons); every Next:, Tonight, Tomorrow and 'Not this week' state, the gold meets-today ring and the 'Houma · tonight' label; the drawer mirroring the viewport, with Search this area and '16 clubs in this area'; the Show regions toggle, the inset region map, its count chips and its hover tooltip; both popovers (the selected pin's, with Directions, Club page and Show card, and the hollow pin's); the seven-row legend panel and '2 programs with no single venue are in the list only'; the 25 and 50 mile rings, the faded far pins, the 'Farther than 75 miles · 17 · Show' bar and the grey far rows; the dashed Gonzales approximate area (it gets a hollow pin at the town); 'Missing a club? A card carries the club's meeting line in the club's own words, or Schedule not listed (7 clubs).' 3 'Location is read once, on tap, and kept only in the address (?near=70808). Clear filters.' S5 Typed 'kni': the list narrows to Knight Light Chess, the New Orleans '8' circle lights, caption '1 club matches kni · Show all 25'. S6 The thin card close-up and the list's last row: 'Gonzales Chess Club · Gonzales / Schedule not listed · Know when they meet? Suggest an update' and beneath it 'Missing a club? Suggest it'. S7 Keyboard: pins are buttons in list order; the drawer is a list; focus on a card lifts its pin; a 'Skip to the list' link sits before the map.

RULES AND DATA (printed as the board's last note). The list always holds all 25; the map never filters it, only Filters do, and they act on both. Sorts: A to Z, and Nearest once located. Location is read once on tap and kept only in ?near=; a typed city or ZIP is sent only to look up a point. No card carries a computed date, a tonight state or a count; the page never computes a next date, a meets-today count, a Meets soonest order or a freshness badge. A card reads clubs.meeting_text (the club's own line, written by the club's representative on its club page) and clubs.schedule_status; filters read clubs.region (Appendix C), clubs.weekend_play and clubs.scholastic_friendly, set by the club on its page; miles come from club_distances (hub to club, road, cached) through a ZIP or city to point lookup; Suggest an update and Suggest a club write club_reports to the club's representative with the regional seat holder copied, LCA admins while a seat is open. Not on this page: Tonight, Next, Checked months, the monthly email, Get updates, a legend panel, a regions overlay, Search this area, club-manager claims, rosters, leaderboards, member counts.

boards.idea: The map is the picker and the drawer is its index: 21 towns A to Z, each with its club count, each opening to its clubs, so you browse Louisiana by town the way you read the map, and Near me puts the towns in distance order and opens the nearest.
boards.differs: A visitor who never presses Near me reads a short index of towns (Baton Rouge · 2 clubs, Bunkie · 1, DeRidder · 1 … Sulphur · 1) that holds the whole state in one glance, and opens any town to see its clubs; the map's pins wear the same 21 town names, so clicking a town on the map and clicking it in the drawer are the same act. 'Show all 25 clubs' opens every row and turns the index into the full list under town headers. That answers the curious visitor's real question ('is there one in Lafayette?') in one look, without regions as the structure (Clubs-F) and without distance as the structure (Clubs-G), and there is no sort control at all: the index is A to Z, or by distance once a place is known.

boards.spec:
BOARD Give-A (Give-A.dc.html): 1440px wide, about 1480px tall (ceiling 1600), Minimal scope, light; the form and a 390×844 phone frame sit side by side, so the board needs no second board. Drawn state: signed out, arrived from the quiet Give line on the membership page; 'Once' and '$25' selected, 'Put it toward' on General.

R0 TITLE STRIP (board only, 1440×56, cream): 'Page 13 · Give · A · The plain /give page' and, gold-ink, 'K: service-first; people mainly give by taking part; giving is there as an option. One sentence, one form, one link.'

R1 HEADER (WS02, 64px navy): rook + name; Tournaments · Clubs · Scholastic · News · Membership · About ▾ (no section current; /give is a utility page); Search; Donate (drawn in its current state: underlined) · Log in · Join LCA (gold).

R2 PAGE BODY (white, from y = 120): two columns inside the wide wrap: left a 760px column, right the phone frame.
LEFT COLUMN: (a) Heading block (about 160px): gold kicker 'GIVE'; H1 'Give to Louisiana chess'; lead, one sentence at 18px: 'Most people support LCA by joining and playing: dues and entry fees pay for nearly everything a volunteer board and 300+ members do. If you'd like to give beyond that, this is the place, and thank you.' No image, no figure, no urgency. (b) Form card (white k-card, 24px padding, about 460px tall): segmented control 'Once' (on) · 'Monthly'; meta under it 'Monthly gifts let the board plan the season. Cancel any time from your receipt email or My LCA.' Label 'Amount': five chips in one row '$10' · '$25' (on) · '$50' · '$100' · 'Other'; choosing Other reveals a field '$ Any amount' (inputmode numeric) with help '$1 or more'. Label 'Put it toward (optional)': a plain select, default 'General', options 'General' · 'Scholastic program' · 'Equipment'; help 'General lets the board use it where it's needed most. No goals, no targets; the treasurer's report says what each year's gifts paid for.' Gold block button 'Continue to Stripe · $25' (Monthly: 'Continue to Stripe · $25 a month'). Under it, two muted lines with a lock icon: 'You pay on Stripe's secure checkout, which asks for your email and card. LCA never sees or stores your card number.' and 'Your receipt comes by email from LCA, right away.' No name or email fields on this page. Nothing about tax deductibility: a designer note in the board margin (not page copy) reads 'No tax-status line until the board confirms LCA's status (brief WS12).' (c) Where the money goes (cream card, about 110px): document icon, h4 'Where the money goes', 'Every dollar, dues and gifts alike, is in the treasurer's report, [fiscal year], published with the minutes as a web page with a PDF copy.' outline 'Read the report' (the Treasurer's reports list on the Minutes page, which exists today) · link 'PDF'. With no report published: 'The treasurer publishes a report after each fiscal year; the latest is on the Minutes page.' and no buttons. (d) Other ways (about 90px, muted 14px, label 'MOST HELP ISN'T MONEY'): one line of plain links 'Join LCA →' · 'Enter a tournament →' · 'Bring someone to club night →' · 'Volunteer at a scholastic event → (write to LouisianaChess@gmail.com)'; a second line 'Prefer a check? Payable to Louisiana Chess Association, [mailing address: board to supply].'
RIGHT COLUMN, phone frame (390×844, standard chrome: 56px app bar with rook, name and Search; bottom tabs Tournaments · Clubs · Log in · Menu; the dock hides on the Stripe hand-off): the same page stacked: kicker, H1 at 28px, the one sentence, the form card full width with the segmented control, the chips wrapping to two rows ($10 $25 $50 / $100 Other), the select, the gold button, the two lock lines; then the 'Where the money goes' card. Caption: 'Phone · one screen to the button; Other and the select use the native keyboard and picker. Donate is two taps away under Menu (WS02); this page is where it lands.'

R3 TWO STATE FRAMES (under R2, side by side, each about 560×220): (a) 'Monthly, Other amount': segmented on Monthly, the Other chip on with the field showing '$15', select 'Scholastic program', button 'Continue to Stripe · $15 a month', meta 'Cancel any time from your receipt email or My LCA.' (b) 'Thank-you page (/give/thanks, the existing DonationSuccessPage rewritten)': H2 'Thank you'; text 'Your $25 gift to the Scholastic program is in. Your receipt is on its way from LCA to danielle@example.com.'; buttons 'See upcoming tournaments' (navy) · 'Back to Membership' (ghost). No name wall, no share buttons, no second ask.

R4 DESIGN NOTES (board only, about 140px, three columns): '1 · The first sentence says how LCA is really supported; the form comes after it, never above it.' '2 · Four amounts and Other; once or monthly; one optional dropdown with three plain choices and no goal, bar or impact line. Put it toward is a memo the treasurer honours, not a restricted fund with its own accounting.' '3 · Where the money goes is the treasurer's report, the same link the membership page uses.' '4 · Stripe Checkout in payment mode for once and subscription mode for monthly, with the choice as metadata; Stripe collects the email; the receipt is the one email from LCA (WS06 D14), never a second from Stripe.' '5 · No tax claim until the board confirms LCA's status.' '6 · Donate stays in the header and footer as WS02 places it (About menu when the row is tight; two taps on phones).' 'Replaces Member-C.'

R5 FOOTER (80px): 'Louisiana Chess Association · US Chess state affiliate · since 1915' · Contact LCA · Website help · Bylaws & minutes · Donate.

THIN AND EMPTY STATES (text on the board under R3): an Other amount under $1 or blank disables the button and shows '$1 or more' under the field; a failed or cancelled Stripe session returns to /give with the chosen amount and purpose kept and a quiet line 'Nothing was charged. Try again when you're ready.'; a signed-in member's email on file is passed to Stripe so the receipt goes to the right address, and 'Put it toward' remembers the last choice; a monthly giver who returns sees one line above the form, 'You give $15 a month to the Scholastic program · Change or cancel', instead of a second ask. The page has no data behind it, so there is no empty state.

Draw the club as the club would present itself, not as a record LCA vouches for.

Out go the computed "Next: Wed, Oct 7 · 6:00 PM" headlines, the Tonight switch and the on/moved/cancelled states, "Meets today" and freshness loops as the organising idea. The club says how it meets in its own words (its pattern, venue, typical times, where changes are announced, for example "Check our Facebook page before you come"), shown as the club's statement with a quiet "As told by the club, updated September 2026" line.
